sections.content: Use *porque* to give a reason for a recent action. The action is expressed with the *pretérito* *perfecto* and the reason follows porque. This structure lets you explain why someone has called, written or sent a message.

items.spanish: Mi madre ha llamado porque necesita hablar conmigo.
items.english: My mother has called because she needs to speak with me.

items.spanish: He contestado porque he recibido una noticia.
items.english: I have answered because I have received some news.

items.spanish: Mi padre ha escrito porque está preocupado.
items.english: My father has written because he is worried.
We have spoken because we need information.

sections.content: The porque clause does not have to match the tense of the main action: Mi *padre* ha *escrito* porque está *preocupado* pairs a pretérito perfecto action with a present-tense reason, because the worry is happening right now, not just when he wrote.
